ct.lead: dashAI is an open-source project. You can contribute with plugins, with changes to the platform's core or without writing code.
ct.extension.p: New components are not added to the core: they are distributed as plugins (extensions), independent Python packages published on PyPI. Once installed, each plugin works like any built-in component.
ct.extension.s1.s: Depending on the kind of component you want to add.
ct.extension.s2.s: One field per parameter; the interface is generated from it.
ct.extension.s3.s: The package exposes its components under dashai.plugins.
ct.extension.s4.s: The package can then be installed from the interface, without restarting.
ct.extension.more: The complete packaging and publishing procedure is described in the plugin development guide.
ct.core.p: Pull requests are reserved for changes to the core: bug fixes, infrastructure improvements and translations.
ct.core.s1.s: Use an existing one or create one describing the change.
ct.core.s2.s: Clone your fork and create a branch from develop.
ct.core.s3.s: Run uv run pytest and uv run ruff check.
ct.core.s5.s: The team reviews the change and may ask for adjustments before merging it.
ct.change.bug.p: Browse the open issues and pick a bug someone has already reported. Reproduce it locally and propose the smallest change that fixes it, with a test that fails before the fix and passes after.
ct.change.infra.p: Changes to the interface, the job system, the HTTP API or file handling. Open a discussion issue first and split the work into small pull requests, with their documentation.
ct.change.lang.p: The interface is available in Spanish, English, Portuguese, German and Chinese. To add a language, copy the locales/en folder, translate the values and register the language in i18n/index.js.
ct.nocode.p: These contributions are as valuable as code and are credited in the project documentation.
ct.free.cite.p: If dashAI was part of your research, citing it helps sustain its academic funding.
ct.free.case.p: Telling us how you use it in courses, research or institutions helps document the project's adoption.
ct.free.report.t: Report a bug or suggest improvements
ct.free.report.p: A good report states the operating system, the dashAI version and the steps to reproduce the problem.
ct.setup.p: You need it to add components or improve the core. It requires Python 3.11 or later, uv, Node LTS and Yarn.
ct.setup.front: In another terminal, start the interface at http://localhost:3000:
ct.setup.cpu: On machines without an NVIDIA GPU, add --extra cpu to uv sync and to every uv run.
ct.setup.more: GPU variants are described in the setup guide.
ct.cta.p: If you are not sure where to start or want to discuss an idea before coding it, write to us.
ct.cta.discord: Talk with the community and the team
